rows.requirement: Cursors are opaque strings (a Business MAY encode them as stateless keyset tokens)
rows.quote:
Cursors are opaque strings. A
Business **MAY** encode them as stateless keyset tokens.
rows.notes: Renamed in 2026-08-25: the actor term changed from 'implementations' to the defined role 'Business' (this release formalizes capitalized Platform/Business roles throughout the spec). Old quote: "Cursors are opaque strings\nthat implementations MAY encode as stateless keyset tokens." New quote: "Cursors are opaque strings. A\nBusiness **MAY** encode them as stateless keyset tokens." Substance (MAY encode as stateless keyset tokens) and sentence structure are otherwise identical. Opacity is a contract on clients; schema types cursor as string only.

rows.requirement: limit request parameter has minimum 1; when omitted the Business MUST apply a default page size (10 is RECOMMENDED, but the Business MAY choose another value)
rows.notes: REWORDED, flagged for review: the schema literally dropped the "default": 10 keyword. OLD schema (shopping/types/pagination.json#L16-20): "limit": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "default": 10, "description": "Requested page size. Implementations MAY clamp to a lower maximum." } — default 10 was a literal schema default. NEW schema removes the literal default and instead states in prose that the Business MUST apply *a* default page size, with 10 only RECOMMENDED (not required) and the Business MAY choose a different value. This downgrades the specific value "10" from a schema default to a RECOMMENDED prose value, while adding a new MUST that some default be applied. minimum:1 remains schema-enforced; the exact-default-of-10 guarantee no longer exists. Also absorbs the substance of old CAT-007/CAT-008 (fewer-results / MUST NOT assume count) directly into the schema description, duplicating search.md prose.

rows.requirement: limit is a hint; a Business MAY return fewer results than the requested or default page size, including when enforcing its own maximum page size
rows.quote:
The Business **MAY** return fewer results than the requested or default page
size, including when enforcing its maximum page size.
rows.notes:
REWORDED, flagged for review: OLD text: "The `limit` parameter is a requested page size, not a guaranteed count.
Implementations SHOULD accept a page size of at least 10. When the
requested limit exceeds the implementation's maximum, implementations
MAY clamp to their maximum silently — returning fewer results without
error." NEW text drops the "SHOULD accept at least 10" floor entirely (see CAT-006, now DEAD) and the "clamp...silently...without error" framing, replacing it with a more general "MAY return fewer results than the requested OR DEFAULT page size" statement that also covers the new default-page-size mechanism (CAT-005). Same core permission (business may legitimately return fewer than requested) but the specific silent-clamping language is gone and scope is broadened to include the default case.

rows.requirement: A Platform MUST NOT assume the response count equals the requested or default page size
rows.quote:
A Platform **MUST NOT**
assume that the response count equals either value.
rows.notes: REWORDED, flagged for review: OLD quote: "Clients MUST NOT assume the response size equals the requested limit." NEW quote: "A Platform **MUST NOT**\nassume that the response count equals either value." Actor renamed Clients -> Platform, and scope broadened from just the requested limit to "either value" (requested OR the new default page size introduced by CAT-005) — a genuine normative expansion, not just a rename, so classified reworded rather than renamed. Client-side constraint; not server-testable.

notes: 2026-08-25 REORG: docs/specification/catalog/{index,lookup,mcp,rest,search}.md moved to docs/specification/shopping/catalog/{index,lookup,mcp,rest,search}.md. source/schemas/shopping/types/pagination.json moved to source/schemas/common/types/pagination.json (a shared value type promoted to the new common/ tree, confirmed by directory diff); source/schemas/shopping/catalog_lookup.json and catalog_search.json did NOT move (still under source/schemas/shopping/).

DEAD (CAT-006): 'Implementations SHOULD accept a page size of at least 10' (old docs/specification/catalog/search.md#L72) has no surviving equivalent anywhere in 08-25. Grepped the whole docs/ and source/ trees for 'at least 10' and 'page size' (2026-08-30): the only 'at least 10' hits are catalog/lookup.md#L76 (a DIFFERENT, unrelated batch-size SHOULD already covered by CAT-027's context, unchanged since 04-08) and common/location/lookup.md#L57 (an unrelated capability). The 08-25 Page Size section (search.md L69-78) replaces the minimum-floor SHOULD with a default-page-size mechanism (see CAT-005/007/008); no requirement obliges a Business to accept a requested page size of any particular minimum. Treated as a genuine requirement removal, not a rename/reword, because no text anywhere states or implies the old floor.

SECURITY-RELEVANT: no requirement in the 08-25 in-scope files mandates stripping scripts/HTML from product or variant descriptions, same finding as 2026-04-08. Not rowed (no verbatim quote available).

Pagination if/then constraint (has_next_page const true => required cursor) remains the only structurally schema-enforced cross-field rule (CAT-002). Dedup (CAT-015/016), variant-exclusion logic (CAT-017 partial), search input-presence (CAT-009/010), and not-found-HTTP-200 (CAT-019/020) remain PROSE requirements => schema_enforced=false, except where backed by a structural constraint (CAT-017/018, CAT-028, CAT-029..031).

The 2026-08-25 release formalizes capitalized 'Business' and 'Platform' as defined roles; several rows carried forward unchanged in substance now read with this vocabulary in the surrounding (unquoted) prose even where the exact quoted clause did not change (e.g. CAT-009/010/011 in search.md kept 'Implementations', untouched).
